4.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'

5.meaning: '(That) they come into my presence' — ḥaḍara means to be present, to attend, to show up somewhere. With 'me' attached: 'that they be present with me / come near me'.
5.grammar: Present-tense verb, 'they' form: ya- plus the plural -ū means 'they (all)'. The final -ni is the object pronoun 'me' with its long -ī vowel dropped, a common Qur'anic shortening — so the word means 'they …me'. The plural -ū here carries the mood ending, and the object 'me' follows directly.

1.meaning: A particle meaning 'until / up to the point that / so that finally'. It marks an end-limit in time or place, or the goal at which an action culminates.
1.grammar: An indeclinable particle (it has no case endings and never changes form). It introduces the end-point or purpose of what precedes, and when followed by a verb it can give the sense of 'until' or 'so that'.

2.meaning: 'When' — a particle introducing a time or circumstance, generally pointing to something expected or definite to come ('when/whenever it happens'). It sets up a condition or moment whose outcome then follows.
2.grammar: An indeclinable adverb/particle of time; it has no case ending and never changes form. It typically introduces a clause about a future or recurring event ('when …'), and is normally followed by a verb describing what takes place.

3.meaning: He/it came, arrived, or came about — the act of coming into presence or of something occurring.
3.grammar: A past-tense verb with no prefix and no personal suffix, naming a completed act by a third-person masculine singular subject ('he/it came'). All three letters here are root letters: jā spells the first radical plus the lengthened weak middle radical, and the final hamza (ء) is the third root consonant — not an ending. The fatḥa (-a) on that hamza is simply the past-tense vocalization for a 'he' subject sitting on the last root letter; there is no separable suffix.

4.meaning: 'One of them' — aḥad, 'one / a single one,' joined to a pronoun, meaning 'any one / one individual among them.'
4.grammar: A noun meaning 'one (of)' with an attached pronoun 'them' (-hum, here vowelled -humu before the next word). The -a ending on aḥad is the accusative case, typically marking it as the object of a verb or otherwise governed. Together it means 'one of them.'

5.meaning: Death — the ending of earthly life; the state or event of dying.
5.grammar: A definite noun ('al-' = 'the') with the -u (nominative) ending, which typically marks it as the subject — the one doing or being something in the sentence.

6.meaning: 'He said' — to speak, utter, or declare; the basic verb for saying words aloud, from the root meaning speech and utterance.
6.grammar: Past tense. The base verb with a final -a marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he') and completed action ('he said'). The middle root letter (w) appears as a long -ā- inside this hollow verb.
6.root: ق-و-ل (q-w-l) — saying, speech, uttering

7.meaning: Rabb (Lord) joined to 'my': the One who owns, sustains, nurtures, and governs — combining mastery, ownership, and loving cultivation. With the attached 'my' it is an intimate address, 'my Lord.'
7.grammar: A noun, rabb, with the first-person possessive (the original 'my' yāʾ being reduced to a final -i, so 'my Lord'). The word denotes the Master who creates, owns, and lovingly sustains. Used as a heartfelt vocative, calling upon one's Lord.
7.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, sustain, master, be lord over

8.meaning: 'Send me back! / Return me!' — a desperate plea using the verb rajaʿa, 'to return'. The plural command form addressed upward ('return-ye me') is often read as a plural of majesty or an urgent, repeated appeal.
8.grammar: Command (imperative) verb. The i- at the front is just a helping vowel to start the command form. The -ū ending makes the command plural ('you all'), and the final -ni is the object pronoun 'me' with its final -ī dropped: 'return me!'.

1.meaning: 'So that I may / perhaps I…' — laʿalla is a particle of hope and expectation: it introduces something the speaker wishes or anticipates ('it may be that…'). With 'me/I' attached: 'in the hope that I…'.
1.grammar: A particle, not a verb or noun, so it has no tense or case. laʿalla always attaches its subject to itself — here the pronoun -ī ('I'). When 'I' attaches, the particle's own final -a vowel gives way to the i-sound of the pronoun (just as inna becomes innī), so the whole reads laʿallī. The following verb states what is hoped for: 'perhaps I will…'. It signals hope or expectation rather than certainty.

2.meaning: A present/future verb meaning 'I do, I act, I perform' — the first-person form of working or carrying out a deed. The root denotes doing, working, and action.
2.grammar: An ongoing or future action. The a- (hamza) prefix marks a first-person singular subject ('I'). The final -u vowel is the indicative ending, signalling a plain factual statement ('I do') rather than a command or a clause after 'that'.
2.root: ع-م-ل (ʿ-m-l) — to do, work, perform a deed

3.meaning: "Righteous / good / sound" — an active participle describing one who or that which is upright and wholesome and acts rightly; as a description of deeds it means good, virtuous works.
3.grammar: An active participle used as a noun or adjective. The -an ending (tanwīn) marks it as indefinite ('a righteous one / a good deed') and in the accusative case — the form used for a direct object or other complement.
3.root: ص-ل-ح (ṣ-l-ḥ) — to be sound / upright / righteous

4.meaning: A compound particle joining the preposition 'in/about' with the relative pronoun 'what', yielding 'in that which' or 'concerning what' — pointing to the matter or subject about which something is said or done.
4.grammar: A fixed combination of the preposition 'fī' and the indeclinable relative 'mā'. Being particles, neither takes a case ending; the phrase functions as 'in/about what…'.

5.meaning: A verb meaning 'I left / abandoned / forsook' — to leave a thing behind, give it up, or relinquish it.
5.grammar: A past-tense verb. The -tu ending marks the doer as 'I' (first person singular), indicating a completed action ('I left / have left').

6.meaning: An emphatic word of rebuke and refusal, used to sharply cut off a false claim or wrong attitude. It means something like 'No indeed!', 'Absolutely not!', or 'Stop right there!' — both a denial and a deterrent warning.
6.grammar: An indeclinable particle of deterrence and emphatic negation; it has no case endings or conjugation. It functions to reject and rebuke what was just said or assumed, often signaling that the speaker should reconsider.

7.meaning: 'Indeed it (is)…' — the emphatic particle inna ('truly, indeed') with an attached feminine pronoun 'it/she'. inna firmly asserts and stresses the statement that follows.
7.grammar: An emphasis particle (inna) plus an attached pronoun, third person feminine singular (-hā). inna introduces and strengthens a nominal statement, and the suffixed -hā is its 'ism' (the noun governed by inna), which inna places in the accusative case. So although -hā corresponds to the English subject ('indeed it/she …'), grammatically it is the accusative ism of inna, not a nominative subject.

8.meaning: A word, an utterance, a statement — a single spoken thing. In usage it can mean anything from one word to a whole pronouncement or claim that someone voices.
8.grammar: Feminine singular noun (the -a(t) is the feminine marker). The -un ending does two jobs: the -u marks the nominative case, used for the subject of a sentence or after 'is/are'; the -n sound (nunation) marks it as indefinite — 'A word', not 'THE word'.

9.meaning: 'He' — the standalone (independent) pronoun for a single masculine person or thing, used for emphasis or to stand as the subject on its own.
9.grammar: An independent (detached) personal pronoun, third-person masculine singular. It does not take case endings; its fixed final -a is part of the word. It serves to name or emphasize the subject ('He is the one who…').

10.meaning: 'The one who says it' — the active participle of 'to say' ('sayer, speaker') with 'it' attached: the person voicing that utterance, its mere speaker.
10.grammar: An active participle — a noun meaning 'the one doing (the verb)', here 'the one saying'. The -u ending is the nominative case, marking it as the subject or the predicate ('he is the sayer of it'). The -hā suffix is the feminine pronoun 'it/her', referring back to a feminine noun such as 'word'.
10.root: ق-و-ل (q-w-l) — saying, speech

11.meaning: 'And from / and out of / and among.' A connector 'and' joined to the preposition 'from,' which marks origin, source, a starting point, or 'some of' a larger whole.
11.grammar: Two particles: the connector 'wa-' ('and') and the preposition 'min.' 'Min' indicates origin or source ('from'), a starting point, or partition ('some of'). Particles do not change their endings.

12.meaning: Before them / in front of them — referring to what lies ahead of the disbelievers, typically Hellfire or punishment awaiting them.
12.grammar: Conjunction waw followed by warāʾa (behind, in front of, beyond) — a preposition/adverb — with the third-person masculine plural possessive suffix -him. The word warāʾ can mean both 'behind' and 'before/in front of' depending on context. Here it indicates what awaits them (Hell).
12.root: و-ر-ء (w-r-ʾ) — behind, beyond, in front of

13.meaning: A barzakh: a barrier or isthmus — an interval that separates two things and prevents them from mixing or crossing. In Islamic usage it names the intermediate realm between death and resurrection, from which there is no return.
13.grammar: A singular noun. The -un ending marks the nominative case (subject / predicate: 'there IS a barrier') and, with its -n sound, indefiniteness — 'A barrier'. The word itself is a rare four-letter noun, likely borrowed, with no ordinary three-letter Arabic root.
13.root: ب-ر-ز-خ (b-r-z-kh, quadriliteral, possibly a loanword) — barrier, interval

14.meaning: A preposition meaning 'to,' 'toward,' or 'up to' — pointing to the end-point, goal, or limit of a motion, direction, or extent.
14.grammar: A preposition (a small linking word). It governs the noun after it, putting that noun in the genitive case, and points to a destination or limit ('to,' 'toward,' 'as far as').

15.meaning: 'Day' — a span of time. It denotes a day or a definite point/period of time; it links to a following word to specify which day (e.g., 'the day of …').
15.grammar: A masculine noun. Its final -i vowel is the genitive case: it typically appears after a preposition or when the word is linked to a following noun in an 'of …' relationship (as in 'the day OF …').

16.meaning: A present-tense verb in the passive meaning 'they are raised up / resurrected / sent forth' — being brought back to life and roused from the dead.
16.grammar: A present-tense passive verb: the yu- prefix with the inner vowel pattern shows the action is done TO the subject ('are raised'), not by them. The -ūna ending marks a masculine-plural 'they' and, with its final nūn intact, signals the indicative mood (the plain statement 'they are raised').
16.root: ب-ع-ث (b-ʿ-th) — to send, raise up, resurrect

1.meaning: A connecting phrase meaning 'then when / and when', introducing a circumstance whose occurrence triggers a following response. 'Fa-' links it to what precedes; 'idhā' sets up a 'when … (then) …' condition for something expected to happen.
1.grammar: A particle cluster, not a noun or verb, so it has no case ending. 'Idhā' is a conditional/temporal particle ('when') used for events regarded as bound to occur, and it normally introduces a clause followed by a main response. The prefixed fa- ('then/so') ties the whole condition to the preceding statement.

2.meaning: (It will) be blown — nufikha is a passive verb meaning 'it was blown', referring to the blowing of the trumpet (al-ṣūr) on the Day of Resurrection.
2.grammar: Nufikha is Form I passive perfect (third masculine singular) from root n-f-kh, meaning to blow. Used in the passive because the focus is on the event of blowing, not the blower (Isrāfīl, the angel). Context: 'The trumpet will be blown (nufikha fī al-ṣūr)' — referring to either the first blow (causing death) or the second blow (causing resurrection).
2.root: ن-ف-خ (n-f-kh) — to blow; a blow, a breath

3.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
3.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

4.meaning: The horn or trumpet — the great horn that is sounded; also the natural sense of a horn-shaped instrument blown to summon or signal.
4.grammar: Definite noun ('the trumpet'). The al- prefix means 'the.' The final -i is the genitive case ending, which typically appears after a preposition or links the word to a preceding noun in an 'of' relationship.
4.root: ص-و-ر (ṣ-w-r) — form, shape; here a horn or trumpet

5.meaning: A two-part word: the connective particle 'fa-' meaning 'so', 'then', or 'therefore' (drawing a consequence from what precedes), joined to 'lā', the particle of negation/prohibition. Together they convey 'so do not …' or 'so there is no …'.
5.grammar: 'fa-' is a connector that links a clause to what came before and often signals a result or consequence. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a present-tense verb it commonly forms a prohibition ('do not …') or a simple negation ('not'). It carries no ending of its own.

6.meaning: Kinship ties, lineages, blood relations — plural of nasab, the genealogical bond that links people by descent and gives them claims on one another.
6.grammar: A broken (internal) plural noun — the plural is formed by reshaping the word (nasab → ansāb) rather than adding an ending. The final -a is the accusative case; nouns take a bare -a like this notably after the absolute-negation 'lā' ('no kinship at all') and as objects of verbs.
6.root: ن-س-ب (n-s-b) — lineage, kinship

7.meaning: An adverb of place meaning 'between' or 'among', here joined to the attached pronoun 'them'; together it conveys 'between them / amongst them', signalling something situated in the midst of a group or shared among parties.
7.grammar: An adverb of place (ẓarf) ending in -a, the accusative marker typical of such adverbs, indicating a location or relationship. The attached suffix '-hum' is a possessive/object pronoun meaning 'them' (a group of males or a mixed group).
7.root: ب-ي-ن (b-y-n) — separation, distinction, what lies in the midst

8.meaning: On that day / that day — pointing back to a particular past day already in view; 'a day, at that time.'
8.grammar: A time-word ('day') joined to 'idhin' ('at that time'), together meaning 'on that day.' The '-in' ('tanwīn') compensates for an understood clause ('the day when…'). The form functions adverbially, locating an event at a specific past moment.

9.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
9.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

10.meaning: will not ask one another / they will not question each other. Refers to the absence of mutual questioning — on the Day of Judgement people will be so overwhelmed they will not ask each other.

parts.en: they ask one another, they question each other (Form VI reciprocal, present 3rd plural)

10.grammar: Present-tense verb (mudāriʿ), 3rd person masculine plural, Form VI (tasāʾala — to ask each other, to question one another). Used with a negative particle; the -ūna ending marks 3rd plural indicative.
10.root: س-أ-ل (s-ʾ-l) — to ask; Form VI: to ask one another, to question each other

1.meaning: A compound meaning 'then whoever' or 'so whoever'. It combines 'then/so' with the conditional/relative 'who', introducing whatever person meets a stated condition.
1.grammar: The connector fa- ('then/so', often answering or following a condition) joined to man ('whoever / the one who'), which refers to people and introduces a condition: 'whoever does X…'. man does not change its ending; the clause after it supplies the rest of the meaning.

2.meaning: A past event describing weight: '(it/she) became heavy / weighed heavy'. The root conveys heaviness, and figuratively gravity, substance, or being burdensome.
2.grammar: This is a completed past-tense verb. The -at ending marks a single feminine (or grammatically feminine) subject — 'she/it became heavy'. This ending is the standard sign that the doer of a past action is feminine singular.

3.meaning: Scales, balances, or weighed amounts — the instruments by which weight is measured, or the resulting weights/measures of worth. The plural denotes multiple such balances or the various weighings of deeds.
3.grammar: This is a plural noun of the 'places/instruments' pattern. The -u ending marks the nominative case (used for the subject of a sentence). The attached -hu means 'his/its', marking possession: 'his scales'.

4.meaning: So those / then those are the ones — a connector 'so/then' joined to a demonstrative pointing to a distant or already-mentioned group: 'those people, they (are the ones who)…'.
4.grammar: 'fa-' is a connector meaning 'so/then', often introducing a result or consequence. 'ulā'ika' is a plural demonstrative ('those') pointing to people, typically picking up a previously described group and setting them up as the subject. It is fixed in form and does not change for case.

5.meaning: An independent (standalone) pronoun meaning 'they' (masculine plural). Standing on its own, it typically adds emphasis or marks the group out as the focus ('they, specifically', 'it is they who').
5.grammar: A detached subject pronoun, third person masculine plural. It takes no case endings; the base is hum, and the final vowel appears as -u (humu) as a connecting vowel to ease pronunciation before a following word beginning with a definite article. Standing alone, it commonly emphasises or isolates the subject.

6.meaning: 'The successful / the ones who flourish' — those who attain what they seek and are saved from what they fear. The underlying sense is of prospering, thriving, and winning through to lasting wellbeing and salvation, not merely worldly success.
6.grammar: A definite active participle (Form IV) in the masculine plural: 'the ones who succeed/prosper'. The al- prefix makes it definite ('the'). The -ūna ending marks a masculine plural in the nominative case — the form used for the subject of a sentence or a predicate identifying who someone is.
6.root: ف-ل-ح (f-l-ḥ) — to prosper, succeed, thrive

1.meaning: And whoever / and the one who — a joining word plus a relative pronoun introducing a person (or persons) defined by whatever they do; often sets up a condition ('whoever does X …').
1.grammar: A particle 'and' joined to the relative/conditional pronoun man ('whoever, who'). Man does not change its ending; it refers to people and frequently functions as a conditional, so the verb that follows it typically takes the shortened jussive mood.

2.meaning: A past event describing lightness: '(it/she) became light / was light in weight'. The root conveys lightness, and figuratively triviality, scantiness, or lack of substance.
2.grammar: This is a completed past-tense verb. The -at ending marks a single feminine (or grammatically feminine) subject — 'she/it became light'. The doubled ff belongs to the verb's root. This ending is the standard sign of a feminine singular doer of a past action.

3.meaning: Scales, balances, or weighed amounts — the instruments by which weight is measured, or the resulting weights/measures of worth. The plural denotes multiple such balances or the various weighings of deeds.
3.grammar: This is a plural noun of the 'places/instruments' pattern. The -u ending marks the nominative case (used for the subject of a sentence). The attached -hu means 'his/its', marking possession: 'his scales'.

4.meaning: So those / then those are the ones — a connector 'so/then' joined to a demonstrative pointing to a distant or already-mentioned group: 'those people, they (are the ones who)…'.
4.grammar: 'fa-' is a connector meaning 'so/then', often introducing a result or consequence. 'ulā'ika' is a plural demonstrative ('those') pointing to people, typically picking up a previously described group and setting them up as the subject. It is fixed in form and does not change for case.

5.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
5.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

6.meaning: 'They lost', 'they have suffered loss', 'they ruined themselves' — said of a group of males who have come out as losers, forfeiting or wasting something of value, especially their own selves.
6.grammar: Past-tense verb. The -ū ending means the subject is 'they' (more than one male) and the action is presented as completed: 'they lost'.
6.root: خ-س-ر (kh-s-r) — loss, to lose, to suffer ruin

7.meaning: A noun meaning 'their own selves' or 'themselves' — the plural of 'nafs' (self, soul, person, inner self), joined to the pronoun 'their.' It commonly conveys the reflexive idea of acting upon one's own self.
7.grammar: A noun (a broken/irregular plural of 'nafs') with the attached possessive pronoun '-hum' ('their/them,' masculine plural). The -a case ending before the pronoun is accusative, typically marking the word as the direct object of a verb — i.e. the self upon which the action falls.

8.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
8.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

9.meaning: Jahannam — a proper name for the Fire of punishment in the Hereafter, the abode of torment. It is a name rather than a descriptive common noun.
9.grammar: A proper name. Because it is a special, non-fully-inflecting noun (it does not take tanwīn), it shows the -a ending in places where most nouns would otherwise take -i; here the single -a serves for both accusative and genitive positions. As a name it carries no general dictionary 'meaning' but designates the abode of punishment.
9.root: — (a proper name; commonly treated as having no Arabic triliteral root)

10.meaning: 'Ones who abide / remain forever; everlasting dwellers.' The plural of an active participle describing those who stay, persist, and endure in a state or place without end — abiding permanently.
10.grammar: An active participle in the masculine plural. The -ūna ending marks a sound masculine plural in the nominative case — the form used when such a group is the subject of a sentence or is being described as being in that state.
10.root: خ-ل-د (kh-l-d) — to remain forever, endure, be everlasting

1.meaning: '(It) scorches' — lafaḥa is the searing lick of flame or burning wind against the face or skin: to burn with a direct, blistering blast.
1.grammar: Present-tense verb with the ta- prefix that marks a feminine 'she/it' subject (used for feminine nouns like 'the Fire'). The final -u is the ordinary (indicative) present-tense ending, marking a plain statement of ongoing fact: 'it scorches'.

2.meaning: Their faces — the faces belonging to them; by extension, what faces forward or the very persons themselves.
2.grammar: A plural noun ('faces') with the attached pronoun 'their'. The -a ending is accusative, the case that typically marks the direct object of a verb (the thing being acted upon). The pronoun is here vowelled -humu (rather than -hum) to ease pronunciation before a following word.
2.root: و-ج-ه (w-j-h) — face; direction, aspect, that which faces

3.meaning: The Fire — a definite noun for fire; frequently the term for the blazing punishment of the Hereafter (Hell).
3.grammar: Definite noun: 'al-' is 'the' (its 'l' assimilates into the following 'n', heard as 'an-nār'). The '-u' ending is nominative, the case typically marking the subject of a sentence or the doer of an action.

4.meaning: 'And they.' The opening 'and' joined to the standalone subject pronoun 'they' (a group of males). A standalone pronoun like this typically begins or emphasizes a statement about its referent.
4.grammar: The conjunction wa ('and') with the detached subject pronoun hum ('they,' masculine plural). As an independent (not attached) pronoun, it serves as the subject of a clause and often lends emphasis to the ones spoken about.

5.meaning: 'In it / therein.' A preposition with an attached pronoun: 'in' plus a feminine singular 'it,' meaning 'inside it / within it,' referring back to some feminine or grammatically feminine thing (such as a place).
5.grammar: A prepositional phrase: fī ('in, within') with the attached object pronoun -hā ('it,' feminine singular). The pronoun is the object of the preposition and points back to a previously mentioned feminine noun.

6.meaning: Grimacing ones — kāliḥ describes a face whose lips have shriveled and pulled back from the teeth, a fixed, contorted scowl; plural: 'those with faces set in a burnt grimace'.
6.grammar: An active participle — a noun/adjective meaning 'ones in the state of (grimacing)'. The -ūna ending is the sound masculine plural in the nominative case, used for the subject of a sentence or after 'they are…': 'they (are) grimacing ones'.
6.root: ك-ل-ح (k-l-ḥ) — grimacing, scowling

1.meaning: 'Did not…?' — a particle combining a question with negation, used to ask 'Have I/has he not…?', often expecting agreement or serving as a gentle reminder.
1.grammar: An interrogative prefix 'a-' ('?') joined to the negation 'lam'. 'lam' negates a verb and places it firmly in the past ('did not'), and grammatically puts the following present-tense verb into the jussive (clipped) form. Together they form a rhetorical or confirming question.

2.meaning: A short (jussive) form of the verb 'to be / to become', meaning 'be' or 'does not become / is not'. It expresses being, existing, or coming to be in a clipped form that typically follows a particle such as a negator or a command.
2.grammar: Present-tense verb with the ta- prefix marking a second-person masculine singular ('you') or third-person feminine singular ('it/she') subject. The clipped final consonant (sukun, no vowel) is the jussive/apocopated mood, the form used after negative particles ('did not / was not') or as a command or prohibition.
2.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existing, coming to be

3.meaning: My signs / My verses — clear tokens, proofs, or revealed verses that point to a truth, here belonging to the speaker ('My').
3.grammar: A sound feminine plural noun ('signs') with the attached possessive -ī meaning 'my'. The plural is built with the -āt ending; the long -ī suffix marks first-person singular ownership.
3.root: ا-ي-ي (ʾ-y-y) — a sign, mark, or token

4.meaning: It is being recited or read aloud — said of verses or scripture conveyed by voice, in an ongoing or repeated manner.

parts.en: recite/read aloud (passive stem, root letters t-l + long ā)

4.grammar: A present-tense (imperfect) passive verb in the third person feminine singular ('it/she is recited'). The tu- prefix marks both the present tense and the passive voice ('is being …-ed'), so the doer is unnamed and the focus is on what undergoes the action. The stem -tlā keeps the second root consonant (t) and ends in a long ā written with ى, the shape a weak-final (defective) root takes when no further ending is attached.
4.root: ت-ل-و (t-l-w) — to recite, read aloud, follow

5.meaning: 'Upon you (all)' — the preposition 'upon/on/over' joined to the plural 'you,' indicating something resting on or directed at a group.
5.grammar: The preposition 'ʿalā' ('upon/on/over') in its joined form 'ʿalay-' plus the attached pronoun '-kum' ('you all,' masculine plural). It marks the group as the recipients or target of whatever is laid 'upon' them.

6.meaning: "So you were / then you used to…" — the verb of being in the past tense addressed to a group, joined to a connective; with a following verb it expresses a continuous past habit ("you used to…").
6.grammar: Past-tense verb: the suffix -tum is the built-in subject 'you all', so no separate pronoun is needed. Followed by another verb, kāna + imperfect means a repeated or ongoing past action — 'you used to…'.
6.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existence

7.meaning: with it / by it — a preposition meaning 'with' or 'by means of' joined to a pronoun referring to a single feminine (or grammatically feminine) thing.
7.grammar: The bi- prefix is a preposition meaning 'with', 'by', or 'by means of'. The attached -hā is an object pronoun meaning 'it' or 'her', referring to something feminine in gender. Together they mean 'with it' or 'by means of it'.

8.meaning: You (a group) deny, reject as false, or treat as a lie — to actively brand something or someone untrue rather than merely doubting.

parts.en: you treat as a lie / deny

8.grammar: A present-tense Form II verb (the doubled, intensive pattern), giving the sense of firmly charging something with falsehood. The stem alone is 2nd-person singular; the '-ūna' ending adds plurality, so the 't-' prefix with that ending marks 'you all' (second person masculine plural) acting now or habitually. The '-ūna' (not '-ū') shows the verb stands in its plain, unaltered present state.
8.root: ك-ذ-ب (k-dh-b) — to lie, be false; to deny, call a lie

1.meaning: 'They said' — a group uttered or stated something. Past-tense speech attributed to a plural subject.
1.grammar: A past-tense verb. The -ū ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject, 'they (said)'. It states a completed act of speaking in the past.

2.meaning: Rabb (Lord) joined to 'our': the Master who creates, owns, sustains, and lovingly nurtures, addressed collectively as 'our Lord' — a communal calling upon the Sustainer.

parts.en: accusative ending (vocative of a possessed noun)

2.grammar: The noun rabb with the attached first-person plural pronoun -nā ('our'). It is used as a vocative, calling out 'O our Lord'. Because the noun is possessed (a muḍāf) and called out in the vocative, it takes the accusative; that -a case vowel sits on the doubled consonant before the pronoun. The pronoun -nā shows the address is made by a group.
2.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, sustain, master, be lord over

3.meaning: 'It (feminine) overcame / defeated / prevailed' — the act of gaining the upper hand and conquering an opponent, completed in the past.
3.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb. The suffix '-at' marks a completed action done by a third-person feminine singular subject ('she/it overcame'). The bare past stem without prefixes indicates the deed is finished, not ongoing.

4.meaning: 'Upon us' / 'over us' / 'against us' — the preposition ʿalā ('on, over, upon') with an attached 'us'. It conveys something resting on, incumbent upon, or bearing against the group.
4.grammar: A preposition (ʿalā, 'upon/over') with an attached pronoun, first person plural (-nā, 'us'). When a pronoun is attached, ʿalā shifts to the form ʿalay-. Such prepositional phrases put their pronoun in the object/genitive role.

5.meaning: 'Our wretchedness' — shiqwah is misery, ill-fatedness, the state of being wretched and cut off from felicity (the opposite of saʿādah, blessed happiness). With 'our' attached: the wretchedness that clung to us.
5.grammar: Feminine noun (the -at is the feminine marker) with the possessive pronoun -nā, 'our'. The -u before the pronoun is the nominative case ending, marking the word as a subject: 'our wretchedness (overcame…)'. Possessed nouns like this drop the -n sound because 'our' already makes them definite.

6.meaning: And we were / we used to be — the past-tense of 'to be' with a 'we' subject; often expresses a continuous or habitual past state ('we used to').
6.grammar: The past-tense verb 'to be' prefixed with 'wa-' ('and'). The suffix '-nā' marks a first-person plural subject ('we'); its nūn assimilates into the doubled nūn of the stem 'kunn-' (shown by the shadda), so only the long vowel is written, but the full ending is '-nā'. It describes a state in the completed past.
6.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, to exist, to come to be

7.meaning: 'A people, a folk, a community' — a group of human beings bound together, often by kinship, tribe, or shared standing.
7.grammar: An indefinite collective noun. The -an ending (accusative with tanwīn, the 'n' sound) marks it as the object of an action.
7.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, rise; a standing group, people

8.meaning: Those who are astray / those who have gone astray — a masculine plural active participle in the accusative/genitive, describing the forefathers as misguided.

parts.en: those who are astray / misguided (active participle, accusative pl.)

8.grammar: Ḍāllīna is the masculine plural active participle from ḍ-l-l (to go astray, be misguided). The -īna ending is accusative/genitive plural, here describing the fathers: 'they found their fathers astray'.
8.root: ض-ل-ل (ḍ-l-l) — to go astray, be lost, be misguided

1.meaning: An address to Allah meaning 'Our Lord' — invoking the Sustainer, Master, and Nurturer who creates, owns, provides for, and brings His servants to maturity. 'Rabb' is a rich term: not merely 'lord' but the One who cherishes and governs all that He has made. The attached 'our' makes it a direct calling upon Him.
1.grammar: A noun ('Lord / Sustainer') with an attached possessive pronoun. The -a ending reflects the accusative, used here in the vocative sense (calling out, 'O our Lord') — the implied 'O' (yā) is dropped before a noun joined to a pronoun. The suffix -nā means 'our'. So it reads 'O our Lord / our Lord!'.
1.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, sustain, master; lordship and cherishing care

2.meaning: A command/plea meaning 'bring us out' or 'take us out' — to cause us to exit or emerge from something. It is a request directed to a single addressee asking that 'we' be removed from a place or situation.
2.grammar: A command (imperative) verb in the causative pattern (af'ala), so it means 'cause to go out' rather than simply 'go out'. The bare imperative form addresses a single 'you'. The attached -nā is the object pronoun 'us', the ones to be brought out.

3.meaning: A two-part word: the preposition 'min' ('from / out of / some of') joined to the pronoun 'it' (feminine). Together: 'from it / out of it / of it,' indicating a source or a portion taken from a feminine thing.
3.grammar: A preposition 'min' with the attached pronoun '-hā' ('it/her'), referring to a feminine noun. 'Min' indicates origin, source, or a part taken from a whole; the attached pronoun is in the object form required after a preposition.

4.meaning: A two-part word: the connective 'fa-' ('then', 'so', 'but') drawing a consequence, joined to the conditional particle 'in' ('if'). Together: 'then if …', 'but if …'.
4.grammar: 'fa-' is a connector that signals a result or transition ('then/so'). 'in' is the conditional particle 'if', introducing a supposed condition. Both are indeclinable particles with no case ending.

5.meaning: 'We returned, went back, reverted.' The root means to come back, to return to a place or to a former state, way, or practice. The subject is 'we.'
5.grammar: A past-tense verb (a hollow root whose middle weak letter contracts in this form). The suffix -nā marks the subject 'we' ('we returned / went back').
5.root: ع-و-د (ʿ-w-d) — to return, come back, revert

6.meaning: Then indeed we: 'we' stated with emphasis and a connecting 'then/so'. The particle inna strongly affirms the statement, while the prefix fa- ties it as a consequence to what came before.
6.grammar: The connective fa- ('then, so', often marking a result) prefixed to the emphasizing particle inna ('indeed, truly'), with the attached first-person plural pronoun -nā meaning 'we/us' (the doubled nūn shared between inna and the pronoun is written once as a shadda). After inna a pronoun takes this object-style form. The whole emphatically asserts a statement about 'we' as a consequence.

7.meaning: 'Wrongdoers' (plural) — those who do wrong, act unjustly, or transgress; people who put things out of their rightful place. The root sense is darkness and misplacing what belongs elsewhere.
7.grammar: An active participle ('one who wrongs') in the masculine plural. The '-ūna' ending marks a masculine sound plural in the nominative case, which typically signals the subject of a sentence or a predicate ('are wrongdoers').
7.root: ظ-ل-م (ẓ-l-m) — to wrong, oppress, do injustice

1.meaning: 'He said' — to speak, utter, or declare; the basic verb for saying words aloud, from the root meaning speech and utterance.
1.grammar: Past tense. The base verb with a final -a marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he') and completed action ('he said'). The middle root letter (w) appears as a long -ā- inside this hollow verb.

2.meaning: 'Be off, despised!' — khasaʾa is the word used to drive away a dog: to repel with contempt. As a command to people it means 'remain there, spurned and disgraced — do not address me', the harshest dismissal.
2.grammar: Command (imperative) verb. The initial i- is only a helping vowel to launch the command form. The -ū ending makes it plural: 'you all'. The silent alif written after the -ū is a spelling convention, not a sound.

3.meaning: 'In it / therein.' A preposition with an attached pronoun: 'in' plus a feminine singular 'it,' meaning 'inside it / within it,' referring back to some feminine or grammatically feminine thing (such as a place).
3.grammar: A prepositional phrase: fī ('in, within') with the attached object pronoun -hā ('it,' feminine singular). The pronoun is the object of the preposition and points back to a previously mentioned feminine noun.

4.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
4.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

5.meaning: '(Do not) speak to Me' — the doubled-middle form kallama means to address someone, to speak TO them. With 'Me' attached: 'address Me'. It appears in the context of a prohibition: speech itself is cut off.
5.grammar: Present-tense verb, 'you (plural)' form of the doubled-middle pattern (Form II) meaning 'address, speak to'. The plural -ū appears WITHOUT the usual -na ending — that dropped -na marks the shortened (jussive) mood used after the prohibiting 'lā' ('do not…'). The final -ni is the object pronoun 'Me' with its -ī dropped.

1.meaning: An emphasis particle fused with a pronoun, meaning 'indeed He' or 'truly He'. The particle inna strongly affirms and certifies the statement that follows ('it is certainly the case that…'), with 'He' as its subject.
1.grammar: The emphasising particle inna ('indeed/truly') with the attached pronoun -hu ('He'). inna affirms and strengthens the whole statement and grammatically takes a following noun or pronoun as its subject. The lengthened -hū is how this pronoun is pronounced after an -u vowel.

2.meaning: He/it was, or there was — the past tense of the verb 'to be', expressing that something existed or used to be the case.

parts.en: to be, was, used to be

2.grammar: A past-tense verb (a 'hollow' verb of being), third-person masculine singular ('he/it was'). The final '-a' marks the ordinary past tense for 'he/it'. Paired with a following present-tense verb, it often conveys 'used to' do something.

3.meaning: A group, party, or faction — a portion or section of people set apart from a larger body.
3.grammar: A masculine singular noun. The '-un' (tanwīn) marks it indefinite ('a group') and in the nominative case, typically used for the subject of a sentence.
3.root: ف-ر-ق (f-r-q) — to separate, divide; a division

4.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
4.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

5.meaning: A phrase meaning 'my servants / my worshippers' — those who serve and worship, bound to a master, with 'my' marking them as belonging to the speaker.
5.grammar: A masculine plural noun, ʿibād ('servants, worshippers', plural of ʿabd), with the attached possessive pronoun -ī ('my'). Before this 'my' suffix the noun's case vowel is replaced by the -i linking sound, so the form reads ʿibādī, denoting 'my servants'.

6.meaning: 'They say / they keep saying' — a present-tense verb of speaking: to say, utter, or assert in words.
6.grammar: Present-tense verb, third-person masculine plural ('they'), from a hollow (middle-vowel) root. The ya- prefix marks the 'they/he' class, the -ū marks the masculine plural subject, and the -na ending signals the ordinary (indicative) present, 'they are saying.'
6.root: ق-و-ل (q-w-l) — speech; saying, uttering, asserting

7.meaning: An address to Allah meaning 'Our Lord' — invoking the Sustainer, Master, and Nurturer who creates, owns, provides for, and brings His servants to maturity. 'Rabb' is a rich term: not merely 'lord' but the One who cherishes and governs all that He has made. The attached 'our' makes it a direct calling upon Him.
7.grammar: A noun ('Lord / Sustainer') with an attached possessive pronoun. The -a ending reflects the accusative, used here in the vocative sense (calling out, 'O our Lord') — the implied 'O' (yā) is dropped before a noun joined to a pronoun. The suffix -nā means 'our'. So it reads 'O our Lord / our Lord!'.
7.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, sustain, master; lordship and cherishing care

8.meaning: We have believed; we have come to faith and trust — to affirm belief, give one's trust, and feel secure in that conviction, stated by a group about themselves.
8.grammar: A past-tense verb on the form-IV pattern (āmana, 'to believe / to have faith'). The ending -nā (a single morpheme, نَا) attached to a past verb marks the subject as 'we'. The doubled 'n' heard in 'āmannā' comes from the verb stem's final 'n' meeting the 'n' that begins the -nā ending.

9.meaning: 'So forgive!' — a command to pardon and cover over wrongdoing, to wipe away faults; when addressed to Allah it is a plea, 'forgive us'. The opening 'so/then' links it to a preceding reason.
9.grammar: A command (imperative) verb addressed to a single person, prefixed by 'fa-' ('so, then'), which connects it to something previously stated as its cause. The verb's bare, vowel-less ending (-ir, with no added vowel) is the form a direct order takes. To 'forgive' here carries the root sense of covering over and concealing a fault.

10.meaning: A combination of the preposition 'for / to' with the pronoun 'us', meaning 'for us' or 'to us / on our behalf'.
10.grammar: A preposition ('for / to') joined to the attached pronoun 'us'. The pronoun -nā always means 'us / our' regardless of position. Together they express benefit or direction toward the speakers ('for us').

11.meaning: A plea addressed to Allah meaning 'and have mercy on us' — an imperative call for divine compassion, tenderness, and relief to be extended to the speakers (a group including the one speaking).
11.grammar: Built on a command (imperative) verb addressed to a single 'You'; when the addressee is the Sovereign, the command takes the sense of humble petition ('please have mercy'). The attached -nā at the end is the object pronoun 'us', so the action is requested upon the speakers. The opening wa- simply joins this to a preceding phrase.

12.meaning: 'And You' — the conjunction 'and' joined to the standalone pronoun 'you' (addressing a single male). The independent pronoun stresses the subject, as in 'and You [Yourself] …'.
12.grammar: A connective 'and' plus a detached subject pronoun. 'anta' is the masculine-singular 'you'; as a standalone pronoun it adds emphasis or introduces a statement about the addressee ('You are …').

13.meaning: 'Best / the best (of)' — superior to all others in goodness, excellence, or worth; the finest in its class.
13.grammar: khayr functions as a comparative/superlative noun ('better / best'). The -u ending marks the nominative case, which typically signals the subject or predicate of a sentence and also opens a possessive phrase ('the best OF …').
13.root: خ-ي-ر (kh-y-r) — goodness, that which is good or best

14.meaning: The merciful ones / those who show mercy — people characterized by compassion and tenderness toward others.
14.grammar: A definite active participle (pattern fāʿil) in the masculine plural ('the merciful ones'). The ending -īna is the plural form used in the genitive or accusative case — typically when the word follows a preposition, is possessed ('… OF the merciful'), or is a direct object.

1.meaning: 'So you took them (as…)' — ittakhadha means to take something and adopt it for oneself: to make it one's own, take it as an object of mockery, worship, or attention. With 'them' attached: 'you made them into (something)'.

parts.en: helping long vowel before the pronoun

1.grammar: Past-tense verb in the self-directed pattern (Form VIII) of 'take': 'take for oneself, adopt'. The -tum ending means 'you all (did)'; when a pronoun like 'them' follows, -tum lengthens to -tumū as a bridge, giving -tumūhum = 'you all took them'. fa- links it as a consequence: 'so/but then'.

2.meaning: As objects of ridicule, as mockery — the state of treating or being treated as something to be laughed at, scorned, or mocked.

parts.en: as an object of ridicule / mockery / derision

2.grammar: A relational adjective (nisba) derived from sukhrī/sikhrī, meaning 'related to ridicule or mockery'. The -an (tanwīn fatḥa) ending is the indefinite accusative, typical of predicates, complements, or adverbial accusatives. The -iyyan (nisba + tanwīn) marks it as an indefinite accusative adjective functioning as a complement: 'as a mockery' or 'for ridicule'.
2.root: س-خ-ر (s-kh-r) — to mock, to ridicule, to subject to scorn; also to subjugate

3.meaning: A particle meaning 'until / up to the point that / so that finally'. It marks an end-limit in time or place, or the goal at which an action culminates.
3.grammar: An indeclinable particle (it has no case endings and never changes form). It introduces the end-point or purpose of what precedes, and when followed by a verb it can give the sense of 'until' or 'so that'.

4.meaning: 'They made you forget' — the causative of 'to forget': not merely that you forgot, but that they were the cause of your forgetting, so absorbed were you in them.
4.grammar: Past-tense verb, 'they' form, in the causative pattern (Form IV): ansā = 'make (someone) forget'. Because the root ends in a weak letter, the plural 'they' ending appears as -aw (instead of -ū). The suffix -kum is the object pronoun 'you all': 'they made you forget'.

5.meaning: 'My remembrance / My reminder' — the act of calling to mind, mentioning, and being mindful, tied to a possessor: remembrance OF me, or my mention of something.
5.grammar: A verbal noun with the attached possessive -ī meaning 'my'. This 'my' ending fixes the word's case, so it reads simply 'my remembrance / my reminder'.
5.root: ذ-ك-ر (dh-k-r) — remembering, mentioning, calling to mind

6.meaning: A verb with attached subject meaning 'and you were' — the past-tense 'to be' for a group, expressing that they existed in or had some state, joined to the connective 'and'.
6.grammar: Past-tense (perfect) verb 'to be', with the attached subject pronoun -tum ('you', masculine plural). The -tum ending names the doers as a group of people addressed ('you all were'). The leading wa- means 'and' or 'while', often introducing a background circumstance ('while you were…').
6.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, to exist, to become

7.meaning: 'Among them / from them / some of them' — the preposition 'min' ('from, of, among') joined to the attached pronoun 'hum' ('them').
7.grammar: The preposition 'min' ('from / of / among') with the attached pronoun 'hum' ('them'), referring to a masculine plural group. Together they often express 'part of them' or 'some among them'.

8.meaning: 'You (all) laugh' — ḍaḥika is ordinary laughter; in the plural 'you' it pictures a group laughing together, and in usage often laughter of mockery at someone.
8.grammar: Present-tense verb, 'you (plural)' form: ta- plus -ūna together mean 'you all'. The full -ūna ending marks the normal (indicative) present tense, describing an ongoing or habitual action: 'you keep laughing'.

1.meaning: 'Truly I' or 'indeed I' — the emphatic affirming particle inna ('truly, indeed, certainly'), which strengthens and confirms a statement, joined to the pronoun 'I'.
1.grammar: An emphasizing particle with an attached pronoun. 'Inna' is a particle of emphasis and affirmation that introduces a statement and lends it certainty ('it is certainly the case that…'). The attached -ī is the first-person singular pronoun ('I / me') in the object form this particle requires. Together: 'Indeed I…'.

2.meaning: 'I have rewarded them / recompensed them' — jazā is to repay someone in full measure for what they did, whether reward for good or requital in general; with 'I' and 'them': 'I have repaid them (their due)'.
2.grammar: Past-tense verb: the -tu ending means 'I (did)' — 'I recompensed'. The suffix -hum is the object pronoun 'them'; its extra final -u is just a helping vowel that appears before certain following words. The stem ends in -ay because the root's weak final letter surfaces as y before consonant endings.

3.meaning: An adverb of time meaning 'the day,' very often used to mean 'today' or 'this day.' With the definite article it points to the present day as a defined, known span of time, and by extension can denote 'now' or 'the present moment.'
3.grammar: A masculine noun carrying the definite article 'al-' ('the'). The final '-a' is the accusative ending; on a noun of time it commonly marks it as an adverb answering 'when?' — fixing the action to that period ('on the day', 'today').
3.root: ي-و-م (y-w-m) — day, a span of time

4.meaning: A compound meaning roughly 'because of what...', 'on account of that which...', or 'by means of what...'. It joins the preposition 'with/by/because of' to a connector 'what/that which', introducing the reason or instrument for something.
4.grammar: A preposition (bi-) fused to the word mā ('what / that which'). The preposition bi- expresses cause, means, or accompaniment; combined with mā it forms a phrase pointing to the thing or fact that serves as a reason or means ('because of what...').

5.meaning: 'They were patient / they endured steadfastly / they persevered.' The verb means to restrain oneself, to bear hardship with calm endurance, to hold firm and not give way to panic or complaint. Ṣabr is steadfast, self-controlled perseverance.
5.grammar: A past-tense verb (Form I) in the masculine plural 'they' person. The stem ṣabar- carries the completed-action (past) sense. The -ū ending marks the doers as 'they' (masculine plural) who performed the act ('they were patient / they endured'). The written alif after it is a silent spelling convention that regularly follows the plural -ū on a verb and is not pronounced.

6.meaning: 'That they…' — an emphatic connector 'anna' ('that, indeed') fused with the pronoun 'they,' used to introduce an affirmed clause as the content of a thought or statement.
6.grammar: Built on the particle 'anna' ('that…, indeed'), which introduces and affirms a following clause (often after verbs of knowing, thinking, or saying) and puts its noun into the accusative. The attached '-hum' is the pronoun 'they/them' for a male-inclusive group.

7.meaning: An independent (standalone) pronoun meaning 'they' (masculine plural). Standing on its own, it typically adds emphasis or marks the group out as the focus ('they, specifically', 'it is they who').
7.grammar: A detached subject pronoun, third person masculine plural. It takes no case endings; the base is hum, and the final vowel appears as -u (humu) as a connecting vowel to ease pronunciation before a following word beginning with a definite article. Standing alone, it commonly emphasises or isolates the subject.

8.meaning: The triumphant, the winners — those who attain what they sought and are saved from what they feared; the truly successful who achieve ultimate salvation and reward.
8.grammar: An active participle ('one who triumphs') with the article 'al-' ('the'), in the masculine plural. The '-ūna' ending marks the nominative plural — the case typically used for the subject or predicate of a sentence ('they are the triumphant').
8.root: ف-و-ز (f-w-z) — to succeed, triumph, win salvation, attain

1.meaning: He said / he spoke — a simple past-tense statement of someone uttering words.
1.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb, third-person masculine singular: 'he said.' The final -a is the standard ending for 'he/it' having done something. The long ā in the stem comes from an original middle root-letter (w) that has shifted to ā in this form.

2.meaning: An interrogative-exclamatory particle meaning 'how many / how much.' It introduces a question or, very often, an exclamation of abundance ('how many a…!'), and is followed by a singular indefinite noun naming what is being counted.
2.grammar: An indeclinable particle (its form never changes for case). In its exclamatory use it asserts a large, indefinite number; in its interrogative use it asks for a quantity. The noun it counts comes next in the singular and indefinite, typically in the genitive (for exclamation) or accusative (for the question).

3.meaning: A verb meaning 'you (all) tarried / remained / stayed' — to linger or abide in a place for a span of time.

parts.en: remained / stayed (stem; all three root letters)

3.grammar: A past (perfect) tense verb. The opening lām is the first radical of the root ل-ب-ث (not a separable particle), so the bare stem is labith- with no prefix. The suffix -tum marks a masculine plural 'you (all)' as those who remained.
3.root: ل-ب-ث (l-b-th) — to tarry, to stay, to remain for a time

4.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
4.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

5.meaning: The earth; the land, ground, or soil. The world we walk upon, as opposed to the sky.
5.grammar: A feminine singular noun with the definite article al- ('the'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('... of the earth') or follows a preposition (as after 'in / on the earth').

6.meaning: Number, count, or sum — the numerical total of a set of things. As the first word of a possessive phrase it gives 'the number OF ...'.
6.grammar: A singular noun. The '-a' ending marks the accusative case (here as object or complement). It is commonly the first term of a possessive pairing, followed by a noun in the genitive ('the number OF the years').
6.root: ع-د-د (ʿ-d-d) — counting, number

7.meaning: 'Years' — the plural of 'year', spans of twelve months. The form is the special plural used for this word when counted or linked to another noun.
7.grammar: A plural noun ('years') taking the sound-plural ending. The '-īna' form is the case used for the object or for a noun linked after a preposition or another noun (the accusative/genitive form of the masculine sound plural), as opposed to the '-ūna' subject form.

1.meaning: 'They said' — a group uttered or stated something. Past-tense speech attributed to a plural subject.
1.grammar: A past-tense verb. The -ū ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject, 'they (said)'. It states a completed act of speaking in the past.

2.meaning: A verb meaning 'we tarried / remained / stayed' — to linger or abide in a place for a span of time.

parts.en: remained / stayed (stem; all three root letters)

2.grammar: A past (perfect) tense verb. The opening lām is the first radical of the root ل-ب-ث (not a separable particle), so the bare stem is labith- with no prefix. The suffix -nā marks a first-person plural 'we' as those who remained.
2.root: ل-ب-ث (l-b-th) — to tarry, to stay, to remain for a time

3.meaning: A day; a defined stretch of time. Often used for a momentous appointed day such as a day of judgement or reckoning.
3.grammar: A singular masculine noun, indefinite ('a day'). The -an ending (tanwīn fatḥa) is the indefinite accusative case, which typically marks the object of a verb or a noun otherwise governed in the accusative.

4.meaning: Or — a particle offering an alternative or another option, linking two possibilities ('this… or that…'). It can also introduce an approximation or a different case.
4.grammar: A fixed connecting particle (a conjunction) with no case ending. It joins two words or clauses to present an alternative between them.

5.meaning: a part of / some of / a portion of — a noun denoting a piece or fraction of a larger whole (in the accusative form).
5.grammar: A noun meaning 'part' or 'some'. The final -a ending is accusative, marking it as a direct object or, with a measure of time, an adverbial span. It is normally followed by a noun in the genitive ('part of …').
5.root: ب-ع-ض (b-ʿ-ḍ) — a part, a portion, some

6.meaning: a day — a day, the basic unit of daytime or a twenty-four-hour span; figuratively a time or occasion.
6.grammar: A singular masculine noun. The final -in ending marks the genitive case together with the indefinite 'a/an'. The genitive is the case used after prepositions or to link this noun to a preceding word ('… of a day').
6.root: ي-و-م (y-w-m) — a day, a span of time

7.meaning: then ask / inquire — a command to put a question or seek information from someone.
7.grammar: A command (imperative) verb addressed to one male, prefixed by fa- ('then, so', signalling a result or sequence). It orders 'ask!'. The final -i here is a connecting vowel added to ease pronunciation into the next word, not a case ending; the bare command is sal/is'al, 'ask'.
7.root: س-أ-ل (s-ʾ-l) — to ask, to question, to request

8.meaning: Those who count or keep a tally — the reckoners, the ones skilled at numbering and calculating. It refers to people whose task or habit is counting things precisely.
8.grammar: An active participle ('one who counts') from the verb ʿadda, 'to count'. The doubling sign (shadda) on the dāl reflects the root's doubled second and third letters (ʿ-d-d), so the word is pronounced with a strengthened d sound. The -īna ending is the sound masculine plural in its accusative/genitive form: it marks 'more than two men/people' when the word is the object of a verb, follows a preposition, or is linked to another noun. So the word as a whole reads 'the counting ones / the reckoners'.

1.meaning: He said / he spoke — a simple past-tense statement of someone uttering words.
1.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb, third-person masculine singular: 'he said.' The final -a is the standard ending for 'he/it' having done something. The long ā in the stem comes from an original middle root-letter (w) that has shifted to ā in this form.

2.meaning: The conditional particle 'in', meaning 'if'. It introduces a hypothetical or supposed condition, setting up a consequence that follows ('if … then …').
2.grammar: 'in' is an indeclinable conditional particle; it carries no case or tense ending of its own. It marks the clause after it as a supposition and leads the listener to expect a result clause.

3.meaning: You stayed, remained, lingered, or tarried; to abide or dwell in a place or state for a stretch of time.
3.grammar: A past-tense verb. The suffix -tum marks a completed action done by 'you all' (a group addressed as males): 'you remained.' This ending is the standard marker for a plural addressee in the past tense.

4.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
4.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

5.meaning: Little, small, scant — small in amount, value, or number; trifling.
5.grammar: An adjective on the stable fa'īl pattern. The -an ending is the indefinite accusative, used here as it describes a noun that is itself accusative ('a little [thing]').
5.root: ق-ل-ل (q-l-l) — to be few, little, scant

6.meaning: A conditional particle introducing a hypothetical or contrary-to-fact supposition: 'if (it were the case that…)'. It typically presents a condition that is unfulfilled or merely imagined, often implying the result did not or would not happen.
6.grammar: An indeclinable particle (no case ending). It signals a hypothetical 'if': it sets up a supposed condition whose consequence is then stated, frequently with the sense 'if X were so, then Y would be so' — often where X is contrary to fact.

7.meaning: 'That you …' — the emphatic particle anna ('that, indeed') fused with the pronoun 'you' (a group); it introduces a firmly asserted statement and points to the addressees as its subject.
7.grammar: The particle anna ('that, indeed'), used to introduce and stress a reported clause, with the attached pronoun -kum ('you,' addressing a group) as its subject. Anna puts a following noun or pronoun in the accusative, and -kum is that fixed object form.

8.meaning: A past-tense verb of 'being' addressed to a group: 'you (all) were', 'you (all) used to be'. From kāna, the core verb 'to be'. With a following predicate it often means 'you were (in a state of) …' or 'you used to …'.
8.grammar: This is a past-tense verb. The '-tum' suffix is the attached subject marker for a masculine plural 'you all'. As the doer is built into the suffix, the verb itself is in its base past form ('you all were').
8.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, to exist, to come to be

9.meaning: A verb addressed to a group: 'you (all) know', 'you have knowledge', 'you are aware'. From the root meaning 'to know'.
9.grammar: The 'ta-' prefix marks a present/future verb addressed to 'you'. The '-ūna' ending marks a masculine plural subject and is the full 'indicative' form, signalling an ongoing, factual statement ('you (all) do know'), as opposed to the shortened '-ū' used after certain particles.

1.meaning: 'Did you then think/suppose...?' — a rhetorical challenge combining a question ('did...?'), a sense of consequence ('then, so'), and the verb 'to reckon or suppose'. The verb ḥasiba means to assume or imagine something to be the case, often mistakenly.
1.grammar: A past-tense verb wrapped in two particles. The a- prefix turns the sentence into a question; fa- adds 'then/so', drawing a conclusion from what precedes. The -tum ending is the past-tense subject marker for 'you (plural, addressing a group)': it tells you the doers of the thinking are 'you all'. Rhetorical a-fa- questions typically imply the assumption was wrong.

2.meaning: A compound particle meaning 'that …' or 'only that' — it introduces and emphasizes a fact as the content of a thought or statement; 'anna' asserts ('indeed/that') and the attached 'mā' often gives a restrictive sense ('that … is only …').
2.grammar: A combination of the emphatic particle 'anna' ('that, indeed') with 'mā'. 'Anna' introduces a noun-clause as the object of verbs like 'think' or 'know', putting the following noun in the accusative. Joined with 'mā' it frequently carries a limiting force, 'only/merely'. Particles like this do not themselves take case endings.

3.meaning: 'We created you' — a past-tense statement that the divine 'We' brought a group into existence, fashioned and originated them. Combines the doer 'We' and the object 'you'.
3.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb with two attached pronouns. The suffix -na is the subject 'we' (the majestic/plural 'We' used of Allah), marking the act as completed. The suffix -kum is the object 'you', addressing a group of males or a mixed group.
3.root: خ-ل-ق (kh-l-q) — creating, originating, bringing into being

4.meaning: In vain, purposelessly, as idle play — ʿabath is aimless activity with no serious purpose or wisdom behind it. Used adverbially it means 'for nothing / uselessly / as a pointless game'.
4.grammar: A noun in the accusative case with the -an ending (written with the extra alif). This -an typically works like English '-ly': it turns the noun into an adverb of manner or purpose — 'uselessly, in vain, for mere play' — describing how or why an action is done.

5.meaning: 'And that you (all)...' — the connector 'and' plus the emphatic particle anna ('that, indeed'), which introduces a firmly asserted fact, with the pronoun 'you (plural)' attached as the subject of that fact.
5.grammar: Wa- is the simple connector 'and'. Anna is a particle meaning 'that', used to report or assert a fact with emphasis; the noun or pronoun after it is put in the accusative. Here the attached pronoun -kum ('you all') is that subject: the whole word sets up a statement about 'you (plural)' — 'and that you...'.

6.meaning: 'To us / toward us' — the preposition 'to/toward' joined to the pronoun 'us,' expressing direction or motion toward the speakers.
6.grammar: Preposition 'ilā' (to/toward), which shifts to the form 'ilay-' before a pronoun, plus the attached pronoun -nā, 'us.' Pronouns after a preposition stand in the genitive (object-of-preposition) role; -nā is a fixed form and does not change shape.
6.root: — (preposition + pronoun)

7.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
7.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

8.meaning: 'You are returned / brought back' — a passive verb from the root meaning to return: the subjects are made to go back, sent back to a point of origin, the action being done to them rather than by them.
8.grammar: Present/future passive. The tu- prefix with the -ūna ending marks a second-person masculine plural subject ('you all'), and the internal vowelling (u–a) makes it passive — the action is done TO the subject. The -ūna ending is the full ('indicative') plural form, used when the verb is not cut short by certain particles.

1.meaning: 'So He is exalted high above (it)' or 'then He is far transcendent.' Built on a verb meaning to be lofty/elevated, this form expresses that someone is utterly high and above something — used of Allah being far beyond any deficiency or false association. The opening fa- links it to what precedes as a consequence.
1.grammar: A 'he' verb expressing height and transcendence. The prefix fa- means 'so/then,' drawing a consequence. The verb pattern intensifies the sense of being elevated and removed far above something lower.
1.root: ع-ل-و (ʿ-l-w) — to be high, lofty, exalted

2.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
2.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

3.meaning: 'The king' — the sovereign ruler who holds dominion and authority over a realm and its people.
3.grammar: A definite noun ('the king'). The final -u ending is the nominative case, the form a noun takes as the subject of a sentence or as a predicate.
3.root: م-ل-ك (m-l-k) — to own, rule, hold dominion

4.meaning: 'The truth / the reality; what is right, real, and rightfully due.' A weighty noun meaning that which is firmly true and real, as opposed to falsehood; it also carries the senses of a rightful claim, a duty owed, and justice. With the article it denotes 'the Truth' in a definite, absolute sense.
4.grammar: A definite noun: the prefix al- ('the') plus the stem. The final -u ending is the nominative case, typically used for the subject of a sentence or for a word identifying what something is (as in 'X is the truth').
4.root: ح-ق-ق (ḥ-q-q) — truth, reality, rightness; that which is established and rightfully due

5.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
5.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

6.meaning: God / object of worship — a deity that is worshipped. The bare noun names the concept of a worshipped god.
6.grammar: A singular noun carrying an -a ending. This short -a typically marks the accusative (object) case; it is also the form a noun takes immediately after the absolute-negation particle 'lā' to mean 'no … (at all).'
6.root: أ-ل-ه (ʾ-l-h) — godhood, worship, being a deity

7.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
7.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

8.meaning: 'He' — the standalone (independent) pronoun for a single masculine person or thing, used for emphasis or to stand as the subject on its own.
8.grammar: An independent (detached) personal pronoun, third-person masculine singular. It does not take case endings; its fixed final -a is part of the word. It serves to name or emphasize the subject ('He is the one who…').

9.meaning: The Lord of — owner, master and sustainer who creates, possesses and governs. Of Allah it names the One who brings up and maintains all that exists.
9.grammar: The noun 'rabb' with the final -u marking the nominative case (subject or predicate: '… is the Lord'). Standing before a following noun it carries the sense 'Lord of …'. It combines ownership, authority and nurturing care.

10.meaning: The Throne — the august Throne, the supreme seat of sovereignty and dominion. As a term it denotes the highest created order and the locus of Allah's majesty and rule over all creation.
10.grammar: A definite noun (al- = 'the'). The final -i ending is the genitive case: the form a noun takes after a preposition or as the second term of a possessive link ('… OF …').
10.root: ع-ر-ش (ʿ-r-sh) — throne, canopy, seat of authority

11.meaning: The Noble, the Generous, the Honorable — karīm describes what is exalted, gracious, and bountiful. Applied to Allah, or to what belongs to Him, it conveys majesty combined with overflowing generosity.
11.grammar: An adjective of the intensive fa'īl pattern, meaning permanently characterized by nobility and generosity. The final -i is the genitive case ending: it typically shows the word follows a preposition or describes (agrees with) another noun that is itself in the genitive — the 'of/with...' case.

1.meaning: And whoever / and the one who — a joining word plus a relative pronoun introducing a person (or persons) defined by whatever they do; often sets up a condition ('whoever does X …').
1.grammar: A particle 'and' joined to the relative/conditional pronoun man ('whoever, who'). Man does not change its ending; it refers to people and frequently functions as a conditional, so the verb that follows it typically takes the shortened jussive mood.

2.meaning: will call
2.grammar: See Arabic text.

3.meaning: With, together with, alongside — indicating company, accompaniment, or being in the same place or time as another.
3.grammar: A preposition of accompaniment ('with, alongside'); grammatically it is an adverbial of place/time (ẓarf) that governs the genitive. It is placed before a following noun to put one thing in the company of another, and that following noun stands in the genitive. The -a is its fixed ending.

4.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
4.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

5.meaning: 'A god / a deity, an object of worship' — the word in its indefinite form, naming a single divine being without specifying which.
5.grammar: A singular indefinite noun. The -an ending combines two things: the accusative case (the form for a verb's object or, often, a noun described by a following adjective) and nunation, the -n sound that signals 'a/an,' i.e. indefiniteness.
5.root: ء-ل-ه (ʾ-l-h) — godhood, that which is worshipped

6.meaning: Another, other, a different one — a further item distinct from the one already mentioned.
6.grammar: An adjective/noun meaning 'other'. It belongs to a small group of words that resist the usual indefinite -n (nunation), so even when indefinite it takes a plain -a ending. That final -a is the accusative case, the form used for a direct object or one in agreement with such a noun.
6.root: أ-خ-ر (ʾ-kh-r) — to be last, come after, other

7.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
7.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

8.meaning: Proof, clear evidence — a decisive, illuminating sign that establishes the truth beyond doubt.
8.grammar: A masculine noun meaning "conclusive proof." The -a ending is accusative, the case used mainly for the direct object of a verb. When such a noun stands as the first term of a possessive construction (iḍāfa), it is made definite by that link and so takes a plain -a without tanwīn.

9.meaning: For him / to him / belonging to him. A small preposition meaning 'to/for' joined to the pronoun 'him', expressing possession, benefit, or direction toward him.
9.grammar: A preposition 'li-' ('to/for') fused with the attached pronoun 'him'. The pronoun 'him' stays the same; it is the preposition that changes, its vowel shifting from -i (li-) to -a (la-) when an attached pronoun follows it directly. The whole unit commonly conveys possession or that something is for someone's benefit.

10.meaning: 'with it,' 'by it,' 'by means of it' — the instrumental/accompaniment preposition 'with/by' joined to 'it' (referring to a masculine singular thing). It marks the means or instrument through which something is done.
10.grammar: A preposition ('with/by') joined to the attached pronoun '-hi' ('it/him'), referring back to a masculine singular thing. The pronoun takes the '-i' vowel form ('hi') because it follows a word ending in an '-i' sound, marking it as the object of the preposition: 'by means of it.'

11.meaning: A compound particle 'so it is only …' or 'then indeed only.' It joins a consequence ('so/then') to an emphatic restriction ('only / nothing more than'), confining the statement to exactly what follows.
11.grammar: A cluster of particles: 'fa-' introduces a result ('so/then'), 'inna' gives emphasis ('truly'), and the attached 'mā' turns the emphasis into restriction, so the whole means 'so it is only/nothing but.' These are connective and emphatic words; they have no case ending of their own.

12.meaning: 'His account' or 'his reckoning' — ḥisāb is the settling of accounts, the audit in which deeds are counted and weighed; with 'his' attached it means the reckoning that belongs to or awaits a particular person.
12.grammar: A noun with the possessive pronoun -hu ('his') attached. The -u before the pronoun is the nominative case ending: it typically marks the word as the subject of a sentence — the thing being talked about ('his reckoning is/will be...'). Attaching a pronoun removes the 'the'/'a' marking, since 'his' already makes it definite.

13.meaning: 'With / in the presence of / near' — an adverb of place and relation meaning at, by, in the sight or estimation of someone. It indicates nearness, possession, or what holds in someone's view (as in 'with Allah' = in His sight).
13.grammar: An adverb of place that is always followed by a noun it relates to. It carries a fixed -a ending; this accusative-type vowel is characteristic of such adverbs of place and shows the word is functioning to locate something ('at, near, in the presence of').

14.meaning: His Lord, Master, and Sustainer — the One who owns, nurtures, governs, and brings to completion; expressing both ownership and loving care over the one belonging to Him.
