14.grammar: A masculine noun with an attached possessive pronoun ("his Lord"). The -i vowel on the noun is genitive, here drawn out because of the following possessive suffix -hi ("his"). The suffix -hi means "his," and its i-form follows naturally after an i-vowel.
14.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — lordship, ownership, nurturing and sustaining to completion

15.meaning: An emphasis particle fused with a pronoun, meaning 'indeed He' or 'truly He'. The particle inna strongly affirms and certifies the statement that follows ('it is certainly the case that…'), with 'He' as its subject.
15.grammar: The emphasising particle inna ('indeed/truly') with the attached pronoun -hu ('He'). inna affirms and strengthens the whole statement and grammatically takes a following noun or pronoun as its subject. The lengthened -hū is how this pronoun is pronounced after an -u vowel.

16.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
16.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

17.meaning: A verb meaning 'he succeeds / prospers / attains salvation' — to thrive and reach what is sought while escaping what is feared; ultimate well-being and triumph, including success in the Hereafter.
17.grammar: Present-tense verb (form IV), third-person masculine singular ('he succeeds'). The yu- prefix marks 'he', and the final -u is the indicative ending for a plain present statement.
17.root: ف-ل-ح (f-l-ḥ) — to prosper, succeed, attain, be saved

18.meaning: Definite plural noun/participle: 'the disbelievers, those who reject faith' — those who cover over and deny the truth. The pattern names a whole group defined by this attribute.
18.grammar: A definite active participle ('the rejecters'). The '-ūna' ending is the masculine sound plural in the nominative (subject) case — the form a word takes when it is the doer of an action or the subject of a sentence ('the disbelievers [are/do]…').
18.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover over, reject, disbelieve

1.meaning: And say! / so say!: a command to one person to speak, joined to what precedes by 'and'.
1.grammar: A command (imperative) verb addressed to a single male, 'say!', prefixed with the conjunction 'wa-' ('and'). The bare, vowel-less ending is the normal form for this imperative.

2.meaning: Lord and Master — the One who owns, sustains, nurtures, and has full authority over a thing; a term combining ownership, care, and lordship that goes beyond any single English word.
2.grammar: A noun with the -i (genitive) ending, which typically links the word to a following noun in an 'of / belonging to' relationship, or follows a preposition or oath particle. 'Rabb' denotes a master who owns, sustains, and nurtures what is under his charge.
2.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — lordship, nurturing, mastery and ownership

3.meaning: Forgive! — a plea or command to pardon, to cover over and blot out wrongdoing. It carries the sense of veiling a fault so it is no longer held against the offender.
3.grammar: A command (imperative) addressed to a single person: 'forgive!'. The vowelless final -r reflects the imperative form. It is commonly followed by 'us' or 'for me' to specify whom to pardon.
3.root: غ-ف-ر (gh-f-r) — to cover, conceal, and pardon; mercy that blots out sin

4.meaning: 'And have mercy' — a plea or command to show raḥma: tender, protective, forgiving compassion. As an address to Allah it is the prayer 'and be merciful (to me/us)'.
4.grammar: Wa- is 'and', joining this to a preceding request. Irḥam is the imperative (command/request) form of the verb 'to have mercy', addressed to one person; the silent (vowel-less) ending -m with no final vowel is the normal mark of the imperative. When addressed to Allah, the command form functions as a humble supplication, not an order.

5.meaning: 'And You' — the conjunction 'and' joined to the standalone pronoun 'you' (addressing a single male). The independent pronoun stresses the subject, as in 'and You [Yourself] …'.
5.grammar: A connective 'and' plus a detached subject pronoun. 'anta' is the masculine-singular 'you'; as a standalone pronoun it adds emphasis or introduces a statement about the addressee ('You are …').

6.meaning: 'Best / the best (of)' — superior to all others in goodness, excellence, or worth; the finest in its class.
6.grammar: khayr functions as a comparative/superlative noun ('better / best'). The -u ending marks the nominative case, which typically signals the subject or predicate of a sentence and also opens a possessive phrase ('the best OF …').
6.root: خ-ي-ر (kh-y-r) — goodness, that which is good or best

7.meaning: The merciful ones / those who show mercy — people characterized by compassion and tenderness toward others.
7.grammar: A definite active participle (pattern fāʿil) in the masculine plural ('the merciful ones'). The ending -īna is the plural form used in the genitive or accusative case — typically when the word follows a preposition, is possessed ('… OF the merciful'), or is a direct object.
